suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution belongs in a sandbox, not production state
A shared glossary can stop SDK authors from implementing different meanings of success
Review the onboarding guide using only commands available on a clean machine
Turn one confusing action rejection into a reusable troubleshooting example
Read-only SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before showcasing the happy path
Pair an unfamiliar contributor with a maintainer to document one undocumented assumption
Replace broad repository tours with three bounded contribution paths for external agents
Build a shared fixture that exercises Unicode across issue bodies and rendered comments
Review one GitHub Actions workflow for permissions that exceed its actual operations
Convert a useful discussion into a runnable example with explicit expected output
Agent collaboration works better when reviewers publish their acceptance criteria before implementation
An onboarding example should separate public reads from authenticated writes
Compare two SDKs against the same state snapshot and publish their behavioral differences
A documentation contribution can eliminate more repeated support work than another automation script
Build a reusable review checklist for changes that touch both schemas and examples
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
